translationRepairs: That October Empress Guo was cast aside with an edict declaring her unfit to "maintain the ancestral sacrifices."
That tenth month Empress Guo was cast aside with an edict declaring her unfit to "maintain the ancestral sacrifices."
其十月 is the tenth lunar month; rendering it as Gregorian October is wrong, and neighboring units already use “Nth month,” so the proposed fix restores the source month without other change.
At month's end on renyin in the eighth month of Yongping 8 (65), a total eclipse reached eleven degrees in Dou.
At month's end on renyin in the tenth month of Yongping 8 (65), a total eclipse reached eleven degrees in Dou.
八年十月壬寅晦 names the tenth month; the idiomatic “eighth month” contradicts the Chinese and is correctly replaced by “tenth month.”
Two years later Empress Liang died and her brothers in the Liang clan were put to death.
Two years later Empress Liang died, and Liang Ji and his brothers were executed.
The transmitted text requires Liang Ji: 翼 is an OCR error for 冀 in 梁冀, and 冀兄弟 means Liang Ji and his brothers, not the empress's brothers generically.
That August six provinces were inundated and the Bohai tide surged over the coast.
That eighth month six provinces were inundated and the Bohai tide surged over the coast.
其八月 is the eighth lunar month, not Gregorian August; the chapter’s dating style uses numbered months, and the proposed wording corrects only that error.
The princes had been patronizing scholars and debaters; the year before, a memorial warned that their clients included descendants of convicted men and demanded a vetting process."
The princes had been patronizing scholars and debaters; the year before, a memorial warned that their clients included descendants of convicted men and demanded a vetting process.
The idiomatic paraphrase does not open a quotation, yet ends with a stray closing quote; removing it restores grammatical English without changing meaning.
